## Third session — a survey of inference-time control, started

The group is opening a survey of methods that guide or control a reasoning
model *during* generation rather than retraining it. Fifteen documents were
read in full for it today; the synthesis lives in the analysis section of
`wiki/concepts/overthinking.md` under "Controlling a reasoning model
mid-generation", and is the thing to read first next time rather than this
entry.

**Twelve papers were filed by hand.** Four had been scored and rejected at
0.25 against a 0.6 bar — including *Controllable LLM Reasoning via Sparse
Autoencoder-Based Steering* and *Less is More: Improving LLM Reasoning with
Minimal Test-Time Intervention*. Eight more were already held but had only
ever been read from their abstracts, because they arrived from conference
poster pages that carry no PDF and `backfill` cannot help a paper that has
already been read. Nine of those twelve are now read from the document.

One could not be obtained. *Adaptive Thinking: Large Language Models Know When
to Think in Latent Space* exists only on OpenReview, which returns a
bot-verification page rather than a PDF, and it stays abstract-only.

**The keyword question was settled by measurement rather than argument.** Four
dry runs over one 30-day window: baseline 62; +15 intervention terms 65;
baseline at a 0.35 bar 438; both together 613. Vocabulary is not the binding
constraint — this literature says "overthinking" once in passing and dies at
0.6 whatever the keyword list contains. The terms were added anyway (note
`0046`) and the bar was left alone; the four papers that mattered came in
through `inbox/`, which is what that path is for.

**A provenance defect worth chasing.** The record for *Mechanistic Detection
and Mitigation of Hallucination in Large Reasoning Models* holds no abstract
and no authors — it is one of the title-only records the virtual-site
collector keeps when a run exceeds its detail cap — yet its summary is marked
`read_from: "abstract"` and names *Reasoning Score*, *ReTruthQA*, *RHD* and
*GRPO-R*. The content checks out against arXiv 2505.12886, which carries all
four terms; the provenance claim does not, because there was no abstract to
read. That field exists precisely so that an abstract-only reading can be
redone later, and a claim to have read something absent defeats it. A count of
how far this goes was commissioned and had not returned when this was written.

**Where the reading stands.** Three of the twelve remain queued, and twenty
new concepts were promoted by today's readings — `manifold-steering`,
`activation-patching`, `difference-in-means-direction-extraction` and others,
all vocabulary that arrived with these papers. That is the next session's
work, and it is worth doing before more collection: the survey's own axis
depends on those definitions existing.

## Late additions, and a count worth acting on

The last three readings landed after the entry above and changed the survey's
shape rather than adding to it. *Thinking vs. NoThinking* suppresses the
dominant Thinking-mode SAE feature and gets **+454% length** — the model
compensates. That is a counterexample to the premise under the whole
suppression family, and it is in the addendum on the overthinking note.
Manifold Steering independently reports that unpurified steering backfires as
strength rises, which turns the content-blind/content-adaptive split from a
design preference into a tested failure.

**The provenance audit came back and it is not one record.** Of 453 paper
summaries: **125 claim `read_from: "abstract"` on records whose `abstract`
field is empty.** All 137 empty-abstract records that have been summarised at
all show this; none says anything else. These are title-only records kept by
the virtual-site collector when a run exceeds its detail cap, so the summaries
were written from something — a fetched page, a PDF, or recall — but not from
an abstract this archive holds.

The other direction is clean: **zero** summaries claim `read_from: "document"`
while naming no document or a missing one. That is the more dangerous failure
and it does not occur.

What to do about the 125 is a decision, not a cleanup. Nothing in the queue
can fix it — a task cannot be reopened once render has consumed it — and the
honest options are to re-collect those items so they arrive with abstracts, or
to leave the flag alone and record here that it is unreliable for exactly this
class of record. It is written down so the next session inherits the number
rather than the surprise.
